content.overview: Section 177 requires prescribed classes of companies to constitute an audit committee with a majority of independent directors and an independent chair.
content.glance: Section 177 requires prescribed classes of companies to constitute an audit committee with a majority of independent directors and an independent chair.
content.study: Listed companies and other prescribed public companies must have an audit committee of at least three directors, with independent directors forming a majority, and an independent director as chair. The committee examines financial statements, auditor independence, related-party transactions, inter-corporate loans, valuations, and internal control, and may obtain professional advice. Related-party transactions, other than those excepted, need the committee's approval. A vigil mechanism for directors and employees is mandatory for listed companies and prescribed classes. The board must disclose the composition and the committee's recommendations not accepted, with reasons.
